channel.title: Manuel Castillejo Blog
channel.description: Reporting and analysis on cognitive health, emerging technology and artificial intelligence.

item.title: AI Is Taking Junior Tasks. Teams Need to Redesign How Expertise Is Learned.
item.description: A new Oliver Wyman Forum report finds AI is already doing some tasks junior employees once learned from managers. The management task is not to preserve busywork, but to make the path from assisted work to independent judgment visible.

item.title: AI Can Answer the Question. Teams Still Need to Know Who Knows the Work.
item.description: A new survey of 1,033 U.S. desk workers raises a useful coordination question: when AI replaces a colleague as the first place to ask, teams can lose sight of the expertise they need to rely on.

item.title: AI Can Compare the Scenarios. Teams Still Have to Own the Trade-Off.
item.description: Workday's newly announced Decision Intelligence product points to a useful management discipline: faster scenario analysis only improves work when assumptions, authority and outcomes remain visible.

item.title: AI Does Not Fix Meetings. It Raises the Standard for Them.
item.description: Jabra's new WorkLife 2026 survey reports that more work is expanding even as AI enters daily routines. The practical response is to make meetings accountable decision points, not cheaper containers for more activity.

item.title: When AI Joins the Conversation, Governance Must Follow the Thread.
item.description: A newly reported financial-services survey points to a practical workplace AI problem: control is not about preserving every prompt, but retaining the context needed to review consequential work.

item.title: The Useful AI Metric Is Not Answers Delivered. It Is Escalations Avoided.
item.description: Microsoft's latest HR account points to a more useful workplace AI test: whether a system makes routine work legible while preserving a clear route to human judgment.

item.title: AI Can Speed Up Work. It Cannot Protect Deep Work for You.
item.description: New workplace data show that AI can improve task productivity. The harder question for teams is whether the time gained becomes better work or simply more interruption.

item.title: AI May Spot Cognitive Decline Earlier. The Hard Part Starts After the Signal.
item.description: The NIH's 2026 progress report highlights StateViewer, a tool combining PET imaging and AI to support earlier detection. The point is not to outsource clinical judgment, but to design the next step better.
